questions.question: For a character vector `dept` of department names without missing values, what does `table(dept)` return?
options: One count per observation, listed in the order of the data
The distinct departments in alphabetical order, without counts
One count per distinct department, in alphabetical order
The share of each department, with the shares adding up to 1

questions.question: For two character vectors `gender` and `dept` of equal length, what does the number in row `Female` and column `Sales` of `table(gender, dept)` count?
options: The observations whose gender is Female or whose department is Sales
The observations whose gender is Female and whose department is Sales
All Female observations, whatever their department
The Sales observations as a share of all Female observations

questions.question: A numeric vector `wage` holds 500 wages, almost all different. What does `table(wage)` give?
options: About ten wage intervals, each with the number of wages that fall in it
An error, because `table()` only works for factors and text
The minimum, mean and maximum wage, as for any numeric vector
One count per distinct wage, so almost every count is 1

questions.question: For `x <- c("b", "a", "b", "c", "b")`, which counts does `table(x)` show, in the order R lists them?
For `x <- c("A", NA, "B", "A", NA)`, what does R print for `sum(table(x))`?
For `x <- c("no", "yes", NA, "no")`, what does R print for `as.vector(table(x, useNA = "ifany"))`?
For `f <- factor(c("lo", "hi", "lo"), levels = c("lo", "mid", "hi"))`, what does R print for `as.vector(table(f))`?
For six workers with `g <- c("F", "M", "F", "M", "F", "F")` and `d <- c("Sales", "IT", "HR", "Sales", "IT", "Sales")`, what does R print for `dim(table(g, d))`?
What does R print for `as.vector(table(c(3, 8, 5, 9) > 4))`?
Departments were typed by hand as `c("Sales", "sales", "Sales ", "HR", "Sales")`, where `"Sales "` ends with a space. How many categories does `table()` of this vector have?
A vector `v` holds 1000 observed values of a discrete random variable $X$, with no missing values. What does `table(v) / 1000` estimate?
options: $\mathbb{P}(X\le k)$ for each value $k$ that occurs in `v`
The expected value $\mathbb{E}[X]$ of the random variable
$\mathbb{P}(X=k)$ for each value $k$ that occurs in `v`
$k\,\mathbb{P}(X=k)$ for each value $k$ that occurs in `v`

questions.question: For worker data with vectors `gender` and `dept` (no missing values), which question can `table(gender, dept)` answer that `table(gender)` and `table(dept)` together cannot?
options: How many women work in the Sales department
How many women there are among the workers
How many different departments there are
How many workers there are in total

questions.question: For `x <- c("A", "B", NA, "A")`, which call gives the relative frequencies of the observed categories, adding up to 1?
options: `table(x) / length(x)`
`table(x) / length(table(x))`
`mean(table(x))`
`table(x) / sum(table(x))`

questions.question: For `g <- c("F", "M", "F", "M")` and `d <- c("S", NA, "E", "S")`, what does R print for `dim(table(g, d, useNA = "ifany"))`?
What happens when R runs `table(c("a", "b"), c("x", "y", "z"))`?
options: It recycles `c("a", "b")` to length 3 and counts three pairs.
It fills the missing third value of the first vector with `NA` and counts two pairs.
It stops with the error `all arguments must have the same length`.
It returns a 2-by-3 table with a count of 1 in every cell.

questions.question: For six workers, `g <- c("F", "M", NA, "F", "M", "F")` and `d <- c("S", "S", "E", NA, "E", "S")`. What does R print for `sum(table(g, d))`?
For two character vectors `g` (gender) and `d` (department), where `d` may contain missing values, what does the sum of the counts in the row `F` of `table(g, d)` equal?
options: The number of observations whose gender is `F`, whatever the department
The number of departments in which gender `F` occurs at least once
The share of gender `F` among all the observations in the data
The number of observations with gender `F` and a known department

questions.question: Survey answers `s` take the values `"low"`, `"medium"` and `"high"`. Which call lists the counts in the order low, medium, high?
options: `table(factor(s, ordered = TRUE))`
`table(factor(s, levels = c("low", "medium", "high")))`
`table(sort(s))`
`table(s)`, after reordering the data so that a `"low"` comes first

questions.question: For `x <- c("a", NA, "b", "a")`, what does R print for `c(length(unique(x)), length(table(x)))`?
Seniority codes were stored once as numbers, `n <- c(10, 9, 10, 2)`, and once as text, `s <- c("10", "9", "10", "2")`. What does R print for `c(as.vector(table(n)), as.vector(table(s)))`?
